title: Chan Kim grabs 36-hole lead at OccuNet Classic presented by Amarillo National Bank - PGA TOUR
snippet: Chan Kim holds a one-shot lead through 36 holes at the OccuNet Classic presented by Amarillo National Bank.
extractedText: 18H AGOChan Kim grabs 36-hole lead at OccuNet Classic presented by Amarillo National Bank1 Min ReadDaily Wrap UpChan Kim makes birdie on No. 16 at BMW Charity Pro-AmAChange Text SizeWritten by Staff Chan Kim holds a one-shot lead through 36 holes at the OccuNet Classic presented by Amarillo National Bank.Charting the leader (stats entering week)CategoryChan KimAge362026 Korn Ferry Tour Points ListNo. 35Starts – Wins – Top-10s on Korn Ferry Tour in 20268-0-2Starts – Wins – Top-10s in Korn Ferry Tour Career40-2-5Chan Kim (first/-9)Two-time Korn Ferry Tour winner posts a bogey-free 5-under 65 in the second round, following his opening round 4-under 66Holds third 36-hole lead/co-lead of his Korn Ferry Tour career; 1-for-2 in converting to victories (2023 Albertsons Boise Open presented by Chevron)Enters the week coming off the best result of his 2026 campaign with a T3 at the BMW Charity Pro-Am presented by TD SYNNEX; in total, he owns two top-10 finishes with two additional top-25 finishes in eight starts on Tour this seasonEarned PGA TOUR membership for the first time with a No. 2 finish on the 2023 Korn Ferry Tour Points List, primarily off the strength of his back-to-back victories at the Magnit Championship and Albertsons Boise OpenHeld full membership on the PGA TOUR the past two seasons (2024, 2025), but was left with conditional membership for the 2026 season after a 130th finish in the 2025 FedExCup Fall standingsOwns 86 career starts on the PGA TOUR with five top-10 finishes and 13 additional top-25 finishes; his best result came in the form of a T5 at the 2025 Valero Texas OpenPlayed predominantly on the Japan Golf Tour from 2015 through the end of 2022, winning eight times on the circuit and winning its 2020-21 Order of MeritBorn in Suwon, South Korea, but grew up in Honolulu, HawaiiAdditional notesOn his 30th birthday, Travis Trace (T2/-8), who began the season with conditional Korn Ferry Tour membership, cards an 8-under 62 and establishes a new 36-hole high position (previous 36-hole high position: T6/2025 BMW Charity Pro-Am/finished T7).Alvaro Ortiz (T4/-7), winner of the 2026 UNC Health Championship, cards an 18-hole career and tournament low 9-under 61 (previous 18-hole low score: 62/2026 UNC Health Championship/Round 2).Eighteen-hole leader Ben Carr (T4/-7) posts a 1-under 69, playing his final three holes (Nos. 7-9) 3-over par, including a double bogey on the seventh hole; holds the best 36-hole position of his career on Tour (previous 36-hole high position: T14/2026 Club Car Championship at The Landings Golf and Athletic Club/finished T7).University of Oklahoma product Jase Summy (T11/-5), who finished No. 3 in the PGA TOUR University Class of 2026, makes nine birdies (Nos. 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17, 18) and an eagle on the par-5 sixth en route to a 6-under 64 to make the cut in his professional and Korn Ferry Tour debut.Sponsor exemption John Daly II (T32/-2), son of five-time PGA TOUR winner John Daly, bounces back from an opening 2-over 72 with a 6-under 64 in the second round to make the cut in his professional debut.Of the eight open qualifiers, only Cameron Sisk (T45/-1) makes the 36-hole cut and advances to the weekend.Amateur and Amarillo native Wyatt Provence (T60/E), who is competing as a sponsor exemption, cards a 3-under 67 to make the cut on the number in his first PGA TOUR-sanctioned start.You May Also LikeView AllRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight Arrow6D AGOKohles claims four-shot victory at BMW Charity Pro-AmDaily Wrap Up10H AGOFischer claims four-shot lead after Round 3 at OccuNet ClassicDaily Wrap Up2D AGOCarr fires 64 to take first-round lead at OccuNet ClassicDaily Wrap Up
